f2_observations: architecture/PORTABLE_HOST_HARNESS_AND_DISTRIBUTION_CONTRACT.md requires a final release ZIP with deterministic manifest and SHA-256 hashes.
AI_START_HERE_DO_NOT_SCAN_REPO/02_RELEASE_CONTRACT.json declares CPython >=3.12 stdlib as the baseline runtime.

src/frankenstein2/portable_release_transaction.py is explicitly a preparatory non-executing transaction/state-lineage primitive and binds artifact/manifest SHA-256 identities, but the inspected module does not consume or extract archive member bytes and does not define archive expansion resource budgets.

primary_sources.observed: The documented decompression pitfalls explicitly include disk/memory resource exhaustion from decompression bombs, incomplete extraction after interruption, filesystem limits, and overwrite behavior when extracting the same archive more than once.

The extraction-filter guidance says the secure default does not prevent every unintended behavior; aborted extraction may leave partial output; further verification should limit extracted-file count, total extracted bytes, filename length and per-file size and account for case-insensitive shadowing and duplicate overwrite semantics.

primary_sources.source: PKWARE ZIP File Capacities technical note
primary_sources.observed: ZIP/ZIP64 format capacities are vastly larger than a reasonable local installer budget, including archive sizes on the order of exabytes and file counts in the billions; format capacity is therefore not a safe application resource policy.

primary_sources.source: PKWARE How PKZIP Works in UNIX
primary_sources.observed: ZIP local-header/central-directory metadata includes compression method, compressed size, uncompressed size, CRC and filename, which can support a cheap declared-size preflight but must not be treated as final consumed-byte truth.

source_supported_findings: Archive path confinement and archive resource confinement are separate invariants; a path-safe archive can still exhaust disk, memory, inode/file-count or time budgets.
A deterministic installer needs explicit application-level archive limits rather than relying on ZIP64 or filesystem maxima.

Declared central-directory sizes are useful for fail-fast preflight, but actual streamed decompressed-byte and entry counters remain necessary because archive metadata is untrusted input until verified.
Extraction should occur in a private empty staging root and any abort/resource violation should leave no promoted release root; partial output is a documented failure mode.
Normalized duplicate names and case-insensitive collisions need an explicit fail-closed policy because overwrite/shadow behavior can make a manifest-to-materialized-tree mapping ambiguous.

architecture_hypothesis.name: PortableArchiveBudgetPolicy
architecture_hypothesis.placement_candidate: archive admission/extraction boundary before release_integrity/static-completeness verification and before installer use
architecture_hypothesis.implementation_bias: prefer a small CPython-stdlib validator/extractor contract over a new framework unless E2 mapping falsifies that sufficiency

counterhypothesis: The existing deterministic release manifest plus exact artifact hash may already bind an approved package strongly enough that generic decompression-ratio policy adds little value; if the actual packaging/installer path verifies a trusted exact artifact before extraction and already enforces exact member byte counts and atomic staging, the proposed policy should collapse to tests/receipt instrumentation rather than a new subsystem.
falsifier_next_gate: E2 must inspect the exact release-manifest schema, packaging producer and archive-to-staging consumer. If they already bind exact normalized member set/sizes and enforce streamed extraction limits plus cleanup, record NO_ARCHITECTURE_DELTA. Otherwise map the smallest missing budget contract and hand it to Trigger4 only after the normal evidence ladder.
